mintAuthority.summary: BorrowerOperations issues USDFC against FIL Troves, but a live 2-of-3 Safe controls token ownership and the ProxyAdmin that can replace mint logic.

controls.label: USDFC BorrowerOperations
controls.evidence: Pinned token borrowerOperationsAddress() returns this protocol contract. Official DebtToken source restricts mint() to BorrowerOperations; ordinary minting is governed by FIL Trove rules, not an immutable end-to-end issuance constraint.

controls.label: USDFC owner and ProxyAdmin-owner Safe
controls.evidence: At Filecoin block 6422489, token owner and ProxyAdmin owner are this Safe. getThreshold()=2, getOwners() returns three addresses, paginated modules are empty and guard storage is zero. Signer independence and an enforced upgrade delay are not established.

review.evidence: At Filecoin block 6425379 on 2026-10-03, the token EIP-1967 implementation remains 0x584c1fa4ab299ae8f7154fce5b1bea7bddacfd0b; token owner() and ProxyAdmin owner() both return the same recorded 2-of-3 Safe, whose threshold and three owners were re-read at that pin. Sourcify match 11586794 verifies the deployed implementation's executable runtime against DebtToken.sol compiled with solc 0.7.6, optimizer 100; runtimeMatch is match, not an exact metadata match. Its mint() invokes _requireCallerIsBorrowerOperations(), which requires msg.sender == borrowerOperationsAddress. This resolves the earlier source-to-executable correspondence question without claiming identical compiler metadata. Published September 2026 upgrades demonstrate exercised Safe authority; code audits do not establish signer independence or financial reserve reconciliation. The live SF Yield Vault warns of an investigation into underlying strategies and lists a USDFC vault. This is not proof that core USDFC mint/Trove contracts were exploited; incident impact on those exact controls remains unresolved, so no incident-free fact is inferred. Financial reserve reconciliation is not applicable to native FIL collateral.
unresolvedQuestions: What impact, if any, does Secured Finance's currently disclosed underlying-strategy security incident have on the exact USDFC BorrowerOperations mint path and owner/ProxyAdmin-owner Safe? The primary live warning does not identify affected contracts or resolve core USDFC control impact; no incident-free state is inferred from separate core code audits or the now-established executable source match.

scopedQuestions.question: Is any enforceable delay imposed on this identified Safe's upgrade authority over the exact USDFC token proxy? No enforceable upgrade timelock is established by the current sources; signer independence is separately retained in evidence, not treated as missing control identity.
